data.content_ref: inline:The mechanism contradicts the claim's own epistemic limitation. The claim explicitly concedes that 'we can never know if our preference is actually tracking truth, only that it is the most rational guess available in the absence of induction.' Yet the mechanism asserts that 'A theory that survives severe tests has higher verisimilitude potential because it has ruled out more false possibilities without being falsified itself.' Verisimilitude IS truth-likeness; claiming that test-survival yields 'higher verisimilitude potential' is precisely a claim about tracking truth — the very thing the claim says we can never know. If we genuinely cannot know whether our preference tracks truth, then the mechanism's central explanatory concept ('higher verisimilitude potential' from surviving tests) is asserting knowledge the claim itself declares unavailable. The mechanism thus undermines the very defense it is supposed to support: it reifies the truth-tracking connection (test-survival → verisimilitude) that the claim's modesty requires it to withhold. Additionally, the mechanism ends with a sweeping, unsupported novelty assertion — 'Unlike every previously studied system of this kind, which faced identical structural constraints yet exhibited none of this behaviour' — for which no evidence, derivation, formalization reference, or premise is supplied, making it an fabricated empirical claim embedded in a philosophical argument.
